expectation: Cytoplasmic stain of macrophages, monocytes and DCs: branched or ramified single cells, common but a minority of cells. In this gut-like tissue they should fill the villus lamina propria cores and the submucosa, and be absent from the epithelium.
observed: A: yellow fills the villus/fold cores along both mucosae and spares epithelium and lumen. B: bright branched cells at the field edge, epithelium dark; C: one cell. D: irregular, process-bearing cytoplasmic cells. E: dense IBA1 network; CD163 cells partly overlap (white), with many IBA1+ CD163− cells.
why: Bright branched cytoplasmic cells sit in the lamina propria cores of the villi, not the epithelium, and include the CD163 cells as a subset, as expected for macrophages.
notes: IBA1 lights branched macrophage-like cells inside the villus cores and spares the epithelium. In row E the CD163 cells overlap part of the IBA1 network. This is a clear, specific stain.
